Stated Claim / Post Context:
Prostitution busts plunge 60% — but hookers multiply — in NYC’s infamous ‘Market of Sweethearts’

Scoring illegal sex along Queens' Roosevelt Avenue has never been easier -- as records show a nearly 60% drop in prostitution-related arrests along the seedy strip since soft-on-crime socialist Zohran Mamdani became mayor this year.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Scoring illegal sex along Queens’ Roosevelt Avenue has never been easier — as the number of hookers has multiplied and prostitution-related arrests have plunged by 60% along the seedy strip since soft-on-crime socialist Zohran Mamdani became mayor this year.

John, a 40-year-old Manhattan horndog, said he has no problem schlepping on the subway to the notorious open-air sex bazaar — nicknamed the “Market of Sweethearts” — because the women are “cheap” and cops have their hands tied by lax laws and policies.

There, scantily-clad streetwalkers brazenly solicit passersby around the clock, offering “happy ending” massages and more in front of rows of two-story commercial buildings. Often the activity occurs within sight of cops on patrol.

The hookers walk their wide-eyed customers inside dozens of illegally operating brothels throughout the avenue’s red-light district, which stretches roughly two miles through Jackson Heights and Corona.

“I can get it done for $60 to $80,” boasted John. “In Manhattan . . .  it costs $200 to $300.”

Negotiating a tryst is “super easy,” he added. “They just show up and that’s it, and when I get bored with those women, I head to Flushing.

“The Chinese women charge $60 for sex and $40 for oral sex,” he said. “They’re open to sex without a condom for $100 or more.

“Latinas are more expensive. With the Chinese women, you get 30 minutes; the Latinas are obsessed with watching the clock.”

He said the woman lead customers to a “place upstairs, in very small rooms.”

A Post reporter last week visited Roosevelt Avenue near 90th Street and spotted nine Asian women turning tricks while two others acted as hostesses or managers. They all declined to comment.

However, when the reporter later approached a group of Ecuadorian sex workers, they began competing for his business.

One offered “massages” using “three positions” running $100 for 20 minutes — which included $50 to rent time in a room of a nearby building.

The second woman offered a discount: “I can [give] you the hour for $300. Normally it’s just 15 minutes, but a half hour we can do it for $150. I give you four positions. We can do whatever.”

Clusters of New York City have been inundated with hookers and pimps brazenly operating on public streets since a state statute prohibiting loitering for the purpose of prostitution was repealed by far-left Albany pols in February 2021.

The change in the law has allowed hookers to operate more freely, with cops turning their attention to traffickers, pimps and johns.

NYPD officers reported making 193 prostitution-related arrests along Roosevelt Avenue this year through Sept. 13, records show.

That’s a massive 59% drop from the 468 arrests during the same period the previous year when ex-NYPD captain-turned-mayor Eric Adams and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch led a major enforcement effort dubbed “Operation Restore Roosevelt.” The raids put a major dent in the migrant sex-peddling strip.

Major crimes like murders and shootings along the same corridor are down 3%.

Former state Sen. Hiram Monserrate said there’s no doubt that illegal prostitution and sex-trafficking markets have flourished along Roosevelt Avenue since Mamdani became mayor, largely because Hizzoner is making it more difficult for cops to enforce the law.

“It is becoming apparent that there is less enforcement, and I think that comes from the top.” said Monserrate, now a local Democratic district leader representing the besieged neighborhoods.

“The current formula is not working to keep our community safe. It’s a disaster. The problem has gotten worse, and this administration has done nothing to correct it.”

“Restore, rinse, release — that’s the problem with Roosevelt Avenue,” said a city government official. “The cops catch these johns and put them away, but they pop up like whack-a-mole. Enough is enough. Someone needs to shut it down.”
